S, THIS DAY, THE COURT MADE THE FOLLOWING:
CORAM: THE HON'BLE MS. JUSTICE J.M.KHAZI  ORAL ORDER (PER: THE HON'BLE MS. JUSTICE J.M.KHAZI) Petitioner who is the sole accused has filed this petition under Section 439 of Cr.P.C. seeking regular bail in crime No.35/2023 of Koppal Women PS pending before the Additional District and Sessions Judge, FTSC-1, Koppal for the offences punishable under Sections 363, 343, 376(3) of IPC and Section 4 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (POCSO) in Spl.S.C.No.POCSO No.47/2024.

sentences.text: 2. In support of the petition, petitioner has contended that he is innocent of the offences alleged.
Even if the entire prosecution case is accepted on its face value, the same do not implicate the petitioner.
The alleged offences are not exclusively punishable with death of imprisonment for life.

The allegation that petitioner kidnapped the prosecutrix in broad day light sounds NC:
2024:KHC-D:18108 unnatural and unreliable.
The medical report is inconsistent with the allegations made.
Petitioner is aged 22 years.
He is in juridical custody since 07.07.2023.
He is ready and willing to abide b any condition that may be imposed by this court and offer substantial surety to the satisfaction of the trial court and hence, the petition.
3. Learned HCGP submitted oral objections stating that complainant is the mother of the prosecutrix, who is aged 15 years 4 months.
The father of the prosecutrix is working in a hotel.

Everyday, prosecutrix attend her school from morning till 5.30 p.m. On 30.06.2023 at 9.00 a.m.
prosecutrix left the house.
However, she did not return even after 6.00 p.m.
Therefore, complainant and others searched for her everywhere.
Since petitioner used to speak to the prosecutrix, she suspects that he might have kidnapped the prosecutrix and accordingly, the missing complaint is filed.
3.1 Based on the complaint, case is registered in crime No.35/2023.

During investigation, petitioner and NC: 2024:KHC-D:18108 prosecutrix were secured and it was revealed that on 30.06.2023,
petitioner kidnapped the proecutrix and took her to the house of C.W.10 at Mariyammanahalli of Vijayanagar District and confined her in the said house for 7 days and during this period, he had sexual intercourse with her once.
Both petitioner and prosecutrix were subjected to medical examination.
The statement of the proecutrix is also recorded under Section 164 of Cr.P.C. by the judicial Magistrate.
The Investigating Officer has recorded the statements of the witnesses.
After completing investigation, charge sheet is filed.
It makes out a strong prima facie case.

sentences.text: 2 gravity of the allegations made, the petitioner is not entitled for bail and pray to reject the petition.

4. Heard arguments and perused the records.
5.

It is the specific case of the prosecution that the prosecutrix is born on 06.02.2008 and therefore,
as on the date of the incident she was aged 15 years 4 months.

It is alleged that the petitioner came to be acquainted with the NC: 2024:KHC-D:18108 proecutrix about three years prior to the date of incident, as he was parking his auto rickshaw in front of her house.
They were regularly in touch with each other.
It is alleged that on 30.06.2023, the petitioner enticed away the prosecutrix and took her to the house of C.W.10 at Mariyammanahalli of Vijaaynagar District and stayed for 7 days.
During this period, petitioner forcibly had sexual intercourse with the prosecutrix.
After the complaint was filed, they were secured from the said house and investigation was proceeded with.
6. Already both prosecutrix and petitioner are subjected to medical examination.
The material objects collected are subjected to forensic examination and the report is awaited.
The statement of the prosecutrix is also recorded by the judicial Magistrate under Section 164 of Cr.P.C.
After conducting detailed investigation, charge sheet is filed.
The petitioner is arrested and remanded to judicial custody on 07.07.2023.
Since already charge sheet is filed, the continued custodial presence of the NC: 2024:KHC-D:18108 petitioner is not necessary.
Of course, there is apprehension that in the event of granting bail, the petitioner may threaten or tamper with the witnesses.
He may also abscond.

However, this may be overcome by imposing stringent conditions and accordingly, the following;
ORDER Petition is allowed.

Petitioner/accused is released on bail in crime No.35/2023 of Koppal Women PS, pending before the Additional District and Sessions Judge, FTSC-1, Koppal for the offences punishable under Sections 363, 343, 376(3) of IPC and Section 4 of the POCSO Act in Spl.S.C.No.POCSO No.47/2024, subject to following:
NC: 2024:KHC-D:18108 CONDITIONS

entities.text: Additional District and Sessions Judge, FTSC-1, Koppal
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
a) The petitioner/accused shall execute a personal bond in a sum of Rs.50,000/-
with two sureties for the like-sum.
b) He shall make himself available for the purpose of investigation as and when required and he shall co-operate with the investigation.
c) He shall furnish his residential address proof and shall inform the investigating officer/Court if there is any change in the address.
d) He shall not threaten or tamper with the prosecution witnesses either directly or indirectly.
e) He shall not contact the prosecutrix either directly or indirectly.
